name: Switch to Darce Configuration
summary: From bottom Buggy Choke, when the top player postures or presses up to escape, keep the head and arm, reach the far hand under their stomach, let go of the leg and come out from under to their head: a front headlock, where the D'Arce is attacked next.
description: Learn Switch to Darce Configuration from bottom Buggy Choke: as the top player postures up, keep the head and arm, let go of the leg and come out to a front headlock.
overview:
Switch to Darce Configuration starts underneath side control with the Buggy Choke: the bottom player's arm wraps the top player's head and one arm and connects to their own raised leg. The switch answers one reaction. When the top player postures up, or presses up with both hands, to escape the Buggy, keep the arm around the head and arm and reach the far hand through under their stomach or armpit. Then let go of the leg connection and come out from under: run or spin the legs through and walk the feet away until you are at the opponent's head, with them bent forward on their knees.

That landing is a front headlock, Front Headlock/Top in the graph. The grip change alone does not put the bottom player on top; coming out from under is a separate movement, and it is the part this move counts. The D'Arce is attacked from the front headlock, by Front Headlock to Darce or Darce Setup, so it stays one move away instead of being assumed here.

If the top player stays low and never postures, keep the Buggy. If they free the head and arm as the leg lets go and keep their weight on you, you are left underneath in side control.

attacker.name: Switch to Darce Configuration Attacker
attacker.description: How to execute Switch to Darce Configuration in BJJ. Attacking perspective with setup, execution steps, and counters.
attacker.overview:
You start underneath side control holding the Buggy Choke: your arm around the top player's head and one arm, connected to your raised leg. The switch is for one moment, when they posture up or press up with both hands to escape. Keep the arm around the head and arm, bring your far hand through under their stomach or armpit, then let go of the leg. Now come out from under: run or spin your legs through and walk your feet away until you reach their head, with them bent forward on their knees.

You finish this move in a front headlock, not in D'Arce control. Holding the head and arm from underneath does not reverse the players; coming out to the head does. The D'Arce is your next attack from the front headlock.

If they stay low and heavy, keep the Buggy. If they pull the head and arm free as the leg lets go, you are underneath side control: frame and protect your inside space.
key_principles: The trigger is the top player posturing up or pressing up with both hands to escape the Buggy; do not start the switch against a flat, heavy top player
Keep the arm around the head and arm for the whole switch; the leg connection is the only thing you let go
Reach the far hand under their stomach or armpit before you let go of the leg
Coming out from under is its own movement: run or spin the legs through and walk the feet away until you are at their head
The switch ends at the head in a front headlock; the D'Arce is attacked from there as the next move, not assumed during the switch
setup_requirements: Buggy Choke from bottom side control: your arm around the top player's head and one arm, connected to your raised leg
The top player postures up or presses up with both hands to escape the Buggy
The head and arm are still trapped inside your arm
Space under their stomach or armpit for your far hand as they lift

execution_steps.description: Hold the Buggy and feel for the top player posturing up, or pressing up with both hands, to escape it. That reaction is the trigger. If they stay low and heavy, keep the Buggy rather than starting the switch.
Keep your arm wrapped around their head and trapped arm. This connection stays on through every later step; it is what you take with you to the front headlock.
As they lift, bring your far hand through underneath their stomach or armpit. Their posture is what makes the space for it.
Release the Buggy's connection to your raised leg. Only the leg comes off; the arm around the head and arm stays where it is.
Run or spin your legs through and walk your feet away, rotating out from underneath them instead of staying flat on your back.
Finish the rotation at their head, with them bent forward on their knees: a front headlock, the head and arm still held. Attack the D'Arce from here as the next move.

common_counters.counter: The top player stays low and heavy and never postures, so the trigger does not appear
common_counters.your_response: Keep the Buggy loop and its own attacks; start the switch only when they lift

common_counters.counter: The top player drops back down before your far hand gets under their stomach, closing the space
common_counters.your_response: Keep the leg connection and the Buggy, and wait for the next posture

common_counters.counter: The top player pulls the head and arm free as the leg lets go and settles their weight back on you
common_counters.your_response: The connection is gone: frame and protect your inside space from bottom side control instead of chasing the neck

common_errors.error: Starting the switch while the top player is flat and heavy
common_errors.consequence: There is no space under their stomach and nothing to come out through, so the Buggy is given up for nothing
common_errors.correction: Wait for them to posture up or press up with both hands; that is the trigger

common_errors.error: Letting go of the leg before the far hand is under their stomach or armpit
common_errors.consequence: The loop opens with nothing replacing it, and the top player can clear the head and arm
common_errors.correction: Reach under first, then let go of the leg

common_errors.error: Letting the head and arm go during the rotation
common_errors.consequence: You come out without the connection that makes the front headlock, or stay underneath side control
common_errors.correction: Keep the arm around the head and arm from the first step to the last

common_errors.error: Staying flat on your back after letting go of the leg
common_errors.consequence: Nothing has changed position: the top player is still on top of you
common_errors.correction: Run or spin the legs through and walk the feet away until you are at their head

common_errors.error: Counting the grip change as being on top in D'Arce control
common_errors.consequence: Holding the head and arm from underneath does not reverse the players; you are still on the bottom
common_errors.correction: Treat coming out to the head as its own step, and attack the D'Arce from the front headlock afterwards

training_progressions.description: Start in bottom Buggy with a cooperative partner. The partner postures up on cue; reach the far hand under their stomach, then let go of the leg. Stop there and check that the head and arm are still held.

Add the rotation: run or spin the legs through and walk the feet away until you reach the head, with the partner bent forward on their knees. Check that you finish at the head with the head and arm held.
The partner chooses between staying heavy and posturing up. Keep the Buggy when they stay heavy and switch only when they lift. Count a repetition only when you reach the front headlock.
Rounds start in bottom Buggy. The partner tries to escape by posturing and to clear the head and arm. Score a front headlock reached with the head and arm held; restart when they settle side control.

flashcards.question: From bottom Buggy Choke, what reaction tells you to switch toward the D'Arce?
flashcards.answer: The top player postures up, or presses up with both hands, to escape the Buggy. That lift is the trigger: it makes space under their stomach for your far hand. If they stay low and heavy, keep the Buggy.
flashcards.answer_line: They posture up or press up

plausible: They flatten out and stay heavy
They turn their back to you

flashcards.question: During the switch, what do you keep and what do you let go?
flashcards.answer: Keep your arm around their head and trapped arm the whole way. Let go only of the Buggy's connection to your raised leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep head and arm; release the leg

plausible: Keep the leg; release the head

flashcards.question: Where does your far hand go before you let go of the leg?
flashcards.answer: Under their stomach or armpit, through the space their posture opens. Reach under first, then release the leg, so the loop never opens with nothing replacing it.

flashcards.question: After you let go of the leg, how do you get out from underneath?
flashcards.answer: Run or spin your legs through and walk your feet away, rotating out from under them until you reach their head. The grip change alone leaves you on the bottom.
flashcards.answer_line: Run legs through, walk to the head

trap: Wait for them to roll you over

flashcards.question: Where does Switch to Darce Configuration end in this graph?
flashcards.answer: At the opponent's head in a front headlock (Front Headlock/Top), with them bent forward on their knees and the head and arm still held. The D'Arce is attacked from there as the next move.

flashcards.question: They pull the head and arm free as you release the leg. Where are you?
flashcards.answer: Underneath side control. The connection you needed is gone and they keep their weight on you, so frame and protect your inside space instead of chasing the neck.

flashcards.question: They stay low and heavy and never posture up. What do you do?
flashcards.answer: Keep the Buggy. The switch needs them to lift; without that there is no space under their stomach and nothing to come out through.

plausible: Let go of the leg anyway

attacker.safety_considerations: The Buggy and the D'Arce are both chokes built around the head and arm, so apply pressure progressively and release at the tap. While coming out from under with the head and arm held, move your body around their head rather than twisting their neck to turn them. Partners with neck or shoulder injuries should say so before drilling, and the defender should tap rather than posture hard against a secured neck.

defender.name: Switch to Darce Configuration Defender
defender.description: How to defend against Switch to Darce Configuration in BJJ. Recognition cues, defensive options, and escape strategies.
defender.overview:
You start on top in side control with your head and one arm inside the bottom player's Buggy loop. This switch is set off by your own escape attempt: posturing up, or pressing up with both hands, opens space under your stomach. Watch for their far hand coming under your stomach or armpit, the connection to their leg letting go, and their legs running through as they come out from under toward your head.

If they get there, you are bent forward on your knees in their front headlock with the head and arm still trapped, and the D'Arce is their next attack. Freeing the head and arm as the leg lets go keeps you on top in side control. Staying low gives them no space to switch, but the Buggy itself is still on.
key_principles: Posturing up or pressing up with both hands is what opens the switch: your escape attempt is its trigger
Their far hand reaching under your stomach or armpit is the first sign
The leg letting go is the moment the loop is weakest; free the head and arm then
If they come out from under, you end bent forward in their front headlock with the head and arm still trapped
Staying low denies the switch but leaves the Buggy on; it is not an escape by itself
recognition_cues: Their far hand slides under your stomach or armpit as you lift
The Buggy's connection to their raised leg lets go while their arm stays around your head and arm
Their legs run or spin through and their feet walk away as they rotate out from under you toward your head

defensive_options.action: Stay low and keep your weight on them instead of posturing up
defensive_options.when_to_use: While you are inside the Buggy and have not yet lifted
defensive_options.if_successful: No space opens under your stomach, so they keep the Buggy rather than switching. The Buggy's own choke threat is still there.
defensive_options.risk: Staying in the Buggy is not safe in itself; tap to a secured choke

defensive_options.action: Drop back down onto them before their far hand gets under your stomach
defensive_options.when_to_use: As soon as you feel the far hand reaching under during your posture
defensive_options.if_successful: The space closes and they keep the Buggy rather than coming out to your head
defensive_options.risk: Dropping back down leaves you inside the Buggy; that choke still needs defending

defensive_options.action: Free your head and arm as the leg connection lets go, then settle your weight back into side control
defensive_options.when_to_use: When their leg releases and they have not yet come out from under
defensive_options.if_successful: You keep top side control with the neck free, and they stay underneath
defensive_options.risk: Pulling hard against a loop that is still closed can tighten it

favorable_outcomes.how: Free the head and arm while the leg lets go and settle your weight back on them. They stay underneath and you keep side control.
Stay low, or drop back down before the far hand gets under, so they keep the Buggy instead of coming out to your head. The Buggy itself still needs defending.

common_errors.error: Posturing up or pressing up with both hands to escape the Buggy without protecting the head and arm
common_errors.consequence: That posture is the switch's trigger: it opens space under your stomach for their far hand
common_errors.correction: If you lift, expect the far hand under you and be ready to free the head and arm as the leg lets go

common_errors.error: Ignoring the far hand under your stomach
common_errors.consequence: They have what they need to let go of the leg and come out from under
common_errors.correction: Treat the hand under your stomach as the first sign and react then

common_errors.error: Staying still while they rotate out from under you
common_errors.consequence: You end bent forward on your knees in their front headlock with the head and arm trapped
common_errors.correction: Free the head and arm while the leg is released, before they reach your head

flashcards.question: On top inside the Buggy, what does posturing up give the bottom player?
flashcards.answer: Space under your stomach. Posturing up, or pressing up with both hands, is the trigger for this switch: their far hand reaches under, the leg lets go and they come out from under to your head.
flashcards.answer_line: Space to switch to a front headlock

plausible: A clean escape from the Buggy
A chance to pass to mount

flashcards.question: What are the signs that the Buggy is turning into a front headlock?
flashcards.answer: Their far hand slides under your stomach or armpit, the connection to their raised leg lets go while the arm stays around your head and arm, and their legs run through as they come out from under toward your head.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand under, leg off, legs through

plausible: They reach for your far ankle

flashcards.question: When is the best moment to free your head and arm?
flashcards.answer: As the leg connection lets go. The loop is then held by the arm alone, and freeing the head and arm before they reach your head keeps you on top in side control.

plausible: Before they ever lock the Buggy

flashcards.question: They come out from under and reach your head. Where are you?
flashcards.answer: Bent forward on your knees in their front headlock, with your head and arm still trapped. The D'Arce is their next attack from there.

plausible: Still on top in side control

flashcards.question: Does staying low end the Buggy threat?
flashcards.answer: Staying low gives them no space to switch, but the Buggy is still on: it stops this move, not the choke you are already in.
flashcards.answer_line: No: stops the switch, not the choke

plausible: Yes, the Buggy needs you to posture
Yes, once you are flat it is over
trap: It ends every attack from there

training_progressions.description: The partner holds the Buggy from bottom side control and runs the switch slowly. From top, name each sign aloud: the hand under the stomach, the leg letting go, the legs running through.
The partner releases the leg on cue. Free the head and arm at that moment and settle back into side control. Stop if the loop is still closed around the neck.
The partner chooses when to switch. Practise staying low against posturing up, and notice that every posture gives them the space. Score keeping side control with the neck free.

variants_and_adaptations.description: Some demonstrations never come out from under. After the far hand goes under the stomach and the leg lets go, the legs run through and the D'Arce is locked and finished with the bottom player still on their side or back. The graph has no node for that branch; this move ends at the front headlock.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When the top player postures up and the D'Arce can be locked before coming out; not modelled by this edge

variants_and_adaptations.description: From the first Buggy frame, the bottom player escapes out from under side control (a ghost escape) and goes to the D'Arce from there. Instructional chapter lists name this route; it is a variant of coming out from under, not a separate landing.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When the bottom player can get out from under side control before the top player postures

variants_and_adaptations.variant_name: Roll over to finish on top
variants_and_adaptations.description: With a D'Arce already locked from underneath side control, rolling the opponent over, toward the side where they have no hand posted, ends with the attacker on top. It is a second movement after the grip, not part of this switch.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When a D'Arce is locked from underneath and a finish on top is wanted

position_integration: Switch to Darce Configuration links Buggy Choke/Bottom to Front Headlock/Top. It is the bottom player's answer when the top player postures or presses up to escape the Buggy: keep the head and arm, reach under the stomach, let go of the leg and come out from under to the head. From Front Headlock/Top the graph continues to Darce Control/Top through Front Headlock to Darce and Darce Setup. A failed switch leaves the Buggy in place (Buggy Choke/Bottom); if the top player clears the head and arm and keeps the pin, the attacker stays in Side Control/Bottom.
conditions: Buggy Choke is held from bottom side control: one arm around the top player's head and one arm, connected to the raised leg
The top player postures up or presses up with both hands to escape the Buggy
The head and arm are still inside the bottom player's arm
The far hand can reach under the top player's stomach or armpit as they lift
